The common areas more than make up for that with all of the greenery and neutral tropical business chic decor for working, dining, lounging, or playing a game of backgammon. I utilized the hotel gym (with peloton), the bikes to ride to fashion square, the free morning yoga on the lawn, the hotel bar for both cappuccino and cocktails, and the restaurant for breakfast, lunch, and dinner - it was all great. There's not always someone at the front desk, so they're not as high-touch as other hotels in the area but I prefer my space. I also loved the multiple pools available that had some shaded areas and beautiful little water features. It was full of families, women, and some couples too, but definitely friendly and chill vibes.

findings.title: Robby C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The Scott is one of those places that's just charming and tasteful - not your typical golfy Scottsdale Resort. We had our wedding here after touring 15 venues. One of the main reasons we chose the Scott? The EXCEPTIONAL staff. You get what you pay for, and these people cared and went above and beyond - we worked with Ira and Deborah which we couldn't have been more pleased with. From their servers at our reception, the quality of the bar, compliments we received on the food, it was beyond perfect and worth every penny. Many of our guests absolutely loved the resort, its location, how central it is to everything in the area, and told us it was the best wedding they've been to.

A year later we've decided to have part of our 1 year wedding anniversary with the Scott because of how much we've enjoyed the resort and its staff. Ira and Deborah even reached out once they found out we were coming back to make our experience personal, and of course, they have already gone above an beyond to accommodate our celebration. The Scott isn't corporate yet professional - it's a place that actually cares about its guests. I'm confident you'll love the resort and service they will provide as much as we have.

findings.title: Kelly S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This resort was very nice! The staff were all very pleasant, and the room service dining was fast. The price was wonderful for Scottsdale area especially and the room was so cute and comfortable. There were no hidden fees as well which was great.

findings.title: David R. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Absolute s***show. Our large group flew in from multiple cities to find none of our rooms would be ready for at least two hours. 2 clerks at the front desk are overwhelmed and nasty. Lobby is hot on 100F Arizona day. Nobody is answering the phone. Avoid at all costs. There are too many nice hotels nearby to suffer through this.

findings.title: Ginger B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This place is really beautiful, everything was just gorgeous and the workers here were very nice, customer service here was above and beyond. Loved the salt water pools, beds, everything. There was a wedding during our stay but it seemed very controlled, didn't even bother our stay at all. I want to come back here so bad!!!

findings.title: Arnold B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
WORST EXPERIENCE EVER WITH BOOKING AN EVENT!!!!!!!!!
Never waste your time trying to book an event at this resort. I have called, left messages and finally drove down to the property in person and asked to speak with someone regarding booking an event AND CRICKETS. I was handed a handwritten email address and a business card to scan and link to a form.  SCREW YOU GUYS if you do not want my business, but don't waste a person's time. The fact I keep being told I cannot talk to anyone because they work from home is ridiculous!!!! I was physically standing at their front desk trying to get information on booking a Christmas party for my 150 employees and NO ONE CARED that I was having no luck reaching anyone and I drove to the property. I just got shut down in person.  I also left my business card with the front desk and no return call.  I am lucky... there are another 20 resorts and venues in the immediate area and I am selecting one of those. The Scott's event planning is broken because they don't answer their phones, voicemails nor talk to a person when standing on their property!  I am sick of websites, emails and people hiding out at home and not working!!!!

findings.title: John E. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is a jewel in the desert. The property is beautifully done and the staff was great. The atmosphere is great. The Canal Club has unique drinks and solid vibe with their own cigars by one of the two pools. Really enjoyed the stay.

findings.title: Annette F. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Can't get or find coffee at the bar or restaurant for the last 3 days. Interesting, only at room service. Can't get coffee to enjoy elsewhere on the property. Very disappointed.

findings.title: Lydia T. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I was working in AZ and decided to stay here. My friends love staying here so I thoughts I'd try it out. I brought my daughter with me and needed to drop her off while I was working l, but before check in. The staff was so helpful and friendly and was able to get her into our room early. The ambiance, look and feel of the lobby is very welcoming with a boho style theme. It was a beautiful place to hang out and work, relax or have a cocktail. The Canal club was nice too. The first night we were there the air conditioning in the room wasn't working. We called the front desk and they immediately sent someone over and determined we needed to move rooms. Although inconvenient, they were prompt in helping us and at least we could get into a room with AC. The rooms were nice and clean. We were able to enjoy the pool while we were there. Although the pool was nice (two pools with one having sand like a beach) I thought the furniture and pool area were not very clean compared to others we've stayed at. They didn't service the second pool with food or drinks which wasn't very convenient. The water was very warm and not refreshing.  There are other locations that have a nicer pool experience. Overall, the hotel was nice and the service of the staff was on point.

findings.title: Margaret V. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We really enjoyed our stay at The Scott. The service was excellent, we had a great room with a beautiful view of the pool area. The restaurant had excellent food - though we only sampled the breakfast offerings - and the bar was fun and entertaining. Service with a smile, we'll likely be back.

findings.title: Chris R. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
If you're in a wheelchair, you're not allowed to bathe.  I'm a paraplegic. I need a shower bench. They do not have one.  That's basically all.  

The hotel is gorgeous- no denying it. But I'm in a chair and I enjoy the luxury of not being and smelling gross.  So a shower bench -$80.00 Investment- could save a major lawsuit.   What if I hurt myself.  $80.00 guys. You probably make it back just by my ordering breakfast.

findings.title: Chris B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The Scott is one of my favorite little gems in Scottsdale!  The decore is unique, tranquil, warm, and inviting. The energy coaxes people out from their shell and fosters communication and engagement.  I regularly meet people in the lobby for a quick informal meeting or discussion when a phone call will not fit the bill. 

However the catalyst for this review was unexpected.  I was hungry and ordered something simple. Cheeseburger. However, I got something that even In & Out wouldn't be able to compete with.  The new burger was f-en balls to the wall un real. You freaking murdered it. Good job chef.  Candied bacon and agave sauce, ok just put more crack on that please. Jesus. Unbelievable.  The Canal Club branding in the bun- not even Steak 44 does that $hit- nice touch. Way to make this place even a little bit more bad a$$ than it was before.  Maybe update the fries a little but thats my only thought. See ya next week!!

findings.title: Madison O. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Decided to get away for our Juneteenth weekend break. Moved our reservation from Hotel Adeline to this place because we wanted somewhere a little more relaxing to stay. 

The first thing we noticed upon arrival was the beautiful decor, very well curated lobby/bar/restaurant space with high ceilings. Great for pictures. 

The front desk experience was smooth. 

The room was spacious, with a nice outdoor area. Very cute. The shower tile wasn't the most clean looking & there were dirty hand markings left on the bathroom door, so that wasn't great. But I am a neat freak who is always prepared to do wipe downs of hotels, so it was fine. 

We placed our bags in the room & went to breakfast. The Spanish coffee was great, the food was okay. I recommend sticking to a basic order, none of the unique dishes. The cocktails were great too, get the Helen & Maude!

I think the shuttle offer is so convenient. The folks driving the shuttle were very friendly & the service was quick. 

We took a spin in the old school Chevy (they offer $30 rides) & it was a lovely time. I head wish we had a longer ride though. 

The pool area gets packed during the day, so I woke up early and swam in the morning. It's pretty. 

Tried the morning yoga & really enjoyed myself. It was perfect for beginners or folks who are a little rusty. 

Overall, had a comfortable stay & would come back again.

findings.title: Marissa F. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My boyfriend and I stayed at this resort for 5 days. The hotel was on the smaller side but was incredible gorgeous. The entire staff was so nice and welcoming they helped with res to places and even transportation! They have a shuttle that can take you in town if it's under 3 miles. Seidu and Rocco were excellent and picked us up when we needed them. They really provided the best experience! The location is PRIME. 4 mins drive to most dinners!! This quaint hotel was really special for us! I hope everyone enjoys

findings.title: Joanna N. (5/5)
findings.snippet: While staying at the Scott resort, the highlight was my day at the pool. Jared, who works at the pool, really made my friend and I feel at home. He was very attentive to making us comfortable, constantly, checking in on us, and friendly conversation, and recommending many places in Scottsdale. He really goes above and beyond to make sure the gas at the pool are happy and taken care of. Thank you, Jared!

findings.title: Mike B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Can you tell this to whoever makes the salads at the restaurant not to serve frozen chicken. I come weekly and every time my chicken is frozen. Don't eat at the Canal Club they serve raw, freezing cold chicken. UNSAFE FOOD!

findings.title: Patricia C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The first stop for our Girls Trip was Phoenix.  I'm so glad we selected 3 nights at The Scott Resort and Spa.  The resort was beautiful.  The food and service were amazing!  Chef Jazz came to our table and recommended several dishes.  I'm a picky eater but we all enjoyed everything brought to the table, throughout the stay.  My absolute favorite was the grass-fed beef filet.  There are several unique items on the menu and whether it's breakfast, brunch or dinner, it's all good.  Our servers were Michael, Aria, Ashley and, Benny for an early breakfast on the patio.  Like Chef Jazz, they were all very friendly, attentive and made our dining experiences pleasurable.  To top it off, Cheyenne made a delicious variety of cupcakes for us.  We felt special from the minute we arrived until we left for our flight to Vegas.  Thanks to all for exceeding or expectations from start to finish.  Until we meet again.

findings.title: Angie C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I had an amazing time while visiting the Scott Resort and Spa April 22-25th. The food and service at The Canal Club was excellent. Chef Jazz (EXCELLENT HOSPITALITY) and staff were amazing, as they took special care to make sure our girls trip was EPIC. All of the food I had at the resort was delicious! I especially liked the black bean purée with plantain tostones. I ordered it three times! Also, the beef filet with Cuban spices was superb! In addition to Chef Jazz, I'd like to give a special thanks to the following servers and staff for helping to make our trip so special: Michael for dinner, Ashley from brunch, Aria on the patio, Benny at the bar for breakfast, Cheyenne for the lovely cupcakes and Trey at the front desk. Keep doing a great job!  I hope to see you again!

Angie

findings.title: Jessica H. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Horrible follow up, I don't understand it! I expected a lot more communication and professionalism, even when I was told I would receive calls and someone would reach out, no one has.

findings.title: Steven H. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
The Scott is way overrated.  Do not get Rooms 101, 103, 105 ,107, 151, 153, 155, 157.  We had room 153 which was right next to the service entrance and a very busy street.  The noise was nearly unbearable - delivery trucks, garbage trucks, etc. Starts at 5:30 am and goes through 9 pm.  We stayed 5 nights and from the first night, management kept promising us that they would move us.  We talked with 5 different "managers" and each one said that they would leave a note for their boss- nothing happened.  Try calling the front desk- we let it ring for 15 minutes before we hung up.

The hotel is way understaffed. Maid service goes late into the afternoon.  Don't even think about room service unless you want over an hour wait- restaurant is the same.  Stay out of the hot tub in the afternoon- its gross.

All-in-all it's not worth the money.

findings.title: Angie B. (4/5)
findings.snippet: We enjoyed our visit to the Scout. Delicious and well prepared food in the Canal House,esp. breakfast. The housekeeping staff very helpful. Our service was provided by Quara. I'm sure I misspelled her name, from the B building. The shuttle service was phenomenal! All the drivers courteous. A special thanks to Chase! Always doing his best! We'll definitely come again!

findings.title: Hilary R. (1/5)
findings.snippet: WORST experience at a hotel. The staff could care less about your experince- half the so called King Views are of the parking lot, the rooms are rundown, filthy with paint peeling, weird black streaks and tile coming up in the shower. Forget about room service as they are " too Busy" and ask you to leave a voicemail mail. The gym was dirty with literally poolside drinks left in there for over 48 hours! The rate of the room was listed incorrectly and when approaching them they did not care~ I have never had such a terrible experience at a hotel that claimed to be "4 Stars" um no. We even asked for a toothbrush to be brought to the room and she literally said " I am the only one WORKING so you have to come down" only one person working at the hotel;??? WHAT? Thank god we didn't have an emergency. RUN AWAY from this dump.

findings.title: Soy Sugar Y. (2/5)
findings.snippet: It looks good from far away but not up close. Imagine finding dried blood on the towel after using it, finding hair stuck to the side mirror, or a slow draining sink. Everything looks painted over and stuck. The food at the restaurant was good - bit on the salty side. Would I stay here again? Not for this price and service.

findings.title: Christine S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I am reluctant to post as I had a great massage by Julianne but would regret not sharing my experience with others to prevent the same from happening. I was visiting from out of town with a brunch and spa day on the agenda. Brunch was fantastic- kudos to the staff at Club Canal. We arrived 45 minutes early to La Vidorra to check in and were taken back into the rooms at 1:04 pm, 4 minutes late despite asking us to arrive early. We we're not offered water, tea, etc. during our wait and sat in the reception area. During our time there, we watched the receptionist share with another guest that their daughter could not receive a treatment based on age, but this information was only shared upon arrival. this foreshadowed a lack of information throughout my visit. 

My massage was finished by 1:54, I know that it was less than 55 minutes as I took a picture prior to the massage beginning and I was not even walked back until 1:04. Upon finishing, I asked if there were showers or amenities to utilize and they said no. No changing area or access to the pool or fitness center. 

For the price paid, this was beyond disappointing. I understand it's a small spa now, but lack of communication and customer service were apparent in the reception staff. 

I would recommend booking a spa experience elsewhere that accommodates a more encompassing experience. Thank goodness I am a member at lifetime fitness to gain access to a shower prior to departure later this evening.

findings.title: Gabe F. (3/5)
findings.snippet: I've found the majority of hotels in the Scottsdale area are pretty bad, so I didn't come with high expectations. It met my low/mediocre expectations. The lobby is nice. They unfortunately stopped the updates there. The rest of the "resort" is basically a motel with rooms that don't have functional wifi (don't dare to try doing work), are in need of serious updating and without functional drains. The first floor rooms feel like caves. The second floor rooms have enough natural light and a large balcony. The hallways smell like they spray Abercrombie Fierce cologne in them. The stay is tolerable for a business trip, but I wouldn't come here expecting a resort experience.

findings.title: John C. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
3.5 stars.

The Scott Resort & Spa is a vibrant, Mission-inspired boutique hotel in the heart of Old Town Scottsdale. Bringing together the colors and comforts of old Havana, the edge and flair of New Orleans, and the elegant geometry of Bauhaus, the resort offers a lush retreat in the middle of the desert with 204 guest rooms and suites and two pools - a sand-bottom swimming pool perfect for families and the main lagoon pool with private cabanas and a pool bar. Featuring the iconic lobby lounge bar and signature restaurant, The Canal Club, specializing in traditional American cuisine with a Caribbean twist. The full-service spa, La Vidorra, features six treatment rooms and a range of massages, body treatments, and facials. 

Our experience here was okay/good but could have been better. The check-in process was easy, thanks to Sam and Carolann. They were incredibly kind, helpful, and accommodating. I couldn't have had a more straightforward check-in process. 

The rooms are decent. The ambiance matches the lobby well, and the old Havana aesthetic shows. However, it could have been more impressive for the price per night (up to $700/night). First and foremost, you would expect more amenities and complimentary snacks for a room that costs a minimum of $400. Let alone water. Everything in the room, including the usage of the robes and drinking water, was an additional cost. There was no room in the refrigerator to store any of our drinks because it was filled with add-on drinks. I don't mind spending money on snacks and drinks, but it made the room feel "low-grade" and not the opulence you should expect from a room with a price tag like The Scott. 

Going back to the amenities, there were hardly any. The pool? The "Lagoon?" Mediocre at best. Nothing special about it. Visualize a Holiday Inn. Motel 6. 

That being said, the housekeepers were fantastic. They were very accommodating and quick with any requests (I asked for a shower cap, which was delivered within minutes). The room service was quick as well. We ordered breakfast from The Canal Club (highly recommended), which was at our front door within 30 minutes. 

The view outside of our room was lacking. It was supposed to come with a private terrace, but the bushes barricading our terrace from the outside pathways were in poor condition and very see-through. There was no privacy whatsoever.

Overall, I do not recommend you pay upwards of $700 a night to stay at a hotel that looks like a luxury Holiday Inn. Their restaurant/bar, The Canal Club, is fantastic (highly recommend!), but their hotel, The Scott, is questionable. The entire hotel would be amazing if they put in the same amount of effort and capital as they did for their lobby. Unfortunately, their lobby is all that it goes, and the rest is a bit more scruffy. Do not get deceived!

findings.title: Logan W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Awesome place!!! The spa is wonderful and the lady Jordan was very helpful. This boutique hotel is very lovely with an awesome bar and staff. The Valet was great, and Chase was more than helpful at giving great restaurant spots. I would highly recommend coming in for drinks and the spa, great spot.

findings.title: Cera H. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Gorgeous, stunning lobby and main areas of hotel. The rooms have awnings and trees in front of the windows so the rooms don't get any natural light. Very dark and cave-like, which is disappointing, considering we escape to Arizona to be in the sun

Additionally, the staff are SO RUDE. It's like the front desk staff was in a competition to see who could be the most bitchy. We stayed for 5 days and they were consistently unwilling to even crack a smile

findings.title: Lisa B. (3/5)
findings.snippet: $400 is WAYOver priced for the rooms and the view and very noisy traffic from the road  . They have a fancy littke espresso machine that squirts out 3.5 oz and only 2 pods so good luck with that. In room dining took 45 min to get a pot of coffee delivered. EDIT: it was lukewarm. Later in the day the hallway of this supposedly FINE hotel was scattered with dirty dishes . Disgusting. When I called at 8pm I was told in room dining was busy and that's why they weren't picked up. Really??? On top of that my heat doesn't work in my room it's 45 this morning and my room temp 65. On hold again for now 30 min ( put on hold 5x) waiting to tell someone about it. Disappointing and will not be back .

findings.title: Marta L. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Great service, ambience is top notch. Feels like your somewhere tropical - in the dessert.

findings.title: Marissa P. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We stayed here for the weekend and loved it! We wanted to get out of Flagstaff for one last mini vacation before school starts back up for our children and this was perfect.

There's a beach sand/pool area for children and they loved it! 
Of course, it's the cutest hotel and everything looks so nice! 

Cons: no fridge or microwave in the room.

Pros: each room has a patio with chairs to relax!

findings.title: Dave S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Magical! You have to ask for Rachel. She will make the best Espresso martini ever.  I like it to taste like coffee after dinner, but if you like it sweet, just stir.

findings.title: Zachary H. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
We departed our room early for breakfast Saturday morning and even spent the entire day by the pool hoping that housekeeping would service our room but they did not which forced me to get fresh towels and clean glasses for our room myself.. not very indicative of the service we expect to receive at a "Four-star hotel". Called the front desk to complain and wasn't offered any solution just an apology. We even mentioned the lack of housekeeping service on the way out and were told that this was an additional service that we needed to request in advance.

For a regular motel, I would rate this 4 stars at best, but for a supposed resort they absolutely do not get my recommendation and I won't be staying here again, too pricy for the quality you receive.

findings.title: Charlie S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Nice atmosphere outside and a very nice pool, make that two pools. The rooms are large and the food at the canal club is good!

findings.title: Tim G. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Just adequate, but way overpriced for what you get. Seems to have been recently renovated, so things are looking snazzy, but the devil is in the details and this is definitely not a 4-star resort. The accommodations are decent, comfortable, and well-appointed. But I wouldn't call it "luxury". That's not the real problem, though. It's the abysmal service.

During our 3-day stay, not a single staff member was friendly. In fact, they all seem quite snobby/clique-y and even apathetic or borderline annoyed to do their job - even something as simple as to serve a coffee or beer. Example: we sat for 15 minutes at the patio in plain view of 3-4 bar staff and they just chatted with each other, or stared at their phones long after spotting us sit down. We finally had to approach the bar on our own and ask for beers, and even that seemed to annoy the bartender and not a single server acknowledged us or came to check up on us as our beers and waters ran dry. Not what you'd expect from a "4-star" luxury resort that regularly charges $300/night! This was not an isolated incident, either.

Add to that little things like broken ice machines, sticky doors, inadequate A/C, and you have a 3-star property with a decent pool, at best.

If you're looking for a place to hang by the pool, get ready for a night out, and have a place to crash after partying in Scottsdale, this place will do. But it's sold as a "luxury" resort and it doesn't live up to that promise. We are very well-traveled and have stayed at a huge variety of hotels ranging from 2 - 6 stars. We will definitely not be back here based on the level of service alone.

findings.title: Pal P. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We just spent two nights here for a belated wedding anniversary and really enjoyed the property. 

Pros: very nice staff, in room Nespresso, fast wifi if you need to get any work done, chromecast in rooms, nice ample seating around the property, the two young pool ladies serving 7/26/22 were super nice and friendly, pool menu pricing wasn't outrageous, nicely decorated rooms, comfortable beds, front desk young lady on 7/27/22 at check-in was super nice and accommodating, well manicured landscaping, good drinks at bar.

Minor cons: A/C fan in room rattled a little bit, could have used more Nespresso pods.

We will be back.

findings.title: N. D. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Meh. I've been to the Canal Club before this visit and I loved the decor and vibe of The Scott so decided to plan a stay with some girlfriends. The Scott photographs beautifully but in reality has some issues. 
Here are a list of pros and cons I experienced. 

Pros:
Staff was friendly 

Lobby and common areas were clean and decorated nicely

Food service was fast

Complimentary late check-out

Cons:
No valet present; parking was a hassle

Room was directly across from Chaparral Road and we could hear heavy traffic- more motel vibe than resort 

Our TV was burnt out in some areas making the lighting terrible. 

No microwave in the room

Pool chairs had tears in them

Towels were small and cheap

A/C in the room was weak. The thermostat would not go lower than 65 but it definitely wasn't that cold in our room. 

Overall it was a fine stay but I would never classify this hotel as a "resort". Definitely not worth the money. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone, nor will I stay here again.

findings.title: Lauren K. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Loved this hotel! Everyone who works at The Scott was super nice and friendly! Great customer service all around! The decor is super cute & love the grounds.  Walking through the property they have swings and hammocks, a gaming section with corn hole connect 4 & cute fire pit seating areas. I can't wait to come back when it's a lot cooler!

findings.title: Trish W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This is the cutest, most relaxing resort! My husband and I stayed here for a staycation to mostly hang out at the pool. Haley is the most attentive server by the pool. She brought us the yumiest strawberry tequila drinks. YUM! The rooms are decorated beautifully, they smell AMAZING and the bed and pillows are comfy! LOVE this resort. I will stay here again and often. If you're looking for a romantic place to get away, THIS IS IT!

findings.title: Ana B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
***** READ ALL REVIEWS**++
Couldn't give 0 stars which is what they deserved !!!!!
The service is terrible!!!! The management team from Brandon the general manager to the assistant manager who is rude and just unpleasant to deal with. 
1st They attempted to charge my credit card 3x so after 1st charge (which is what is required for reservation)  I locked and advised GM Brandon since his asst manager Inka- something blamed it on him not knowing what he was doing when HE checked us in.  Our bags were over an hour late to be sent to our room no one was able to help and front desk kept saying sorry we are training new people etc. which is understandable but not something the customer should have to pay for that's a management issue not mine!!   We arrive to our suite parlor and the dining table had peanut butter and bread crumbs and chairs were moved all around with dirt on floor - I call the front desk and they said a manger will come look first. Manager comes in looks and says oh okay we will send someone and dirt on the floor is from the wind outside not crumbs and leaves almost bothered by us calling - cleaning person came wiped it down and left .. The Scott's where the customer is always wrong.  Pool staff same - rude and arrogant not the bartender but Pool attendants..  We order food and drinks (party or 8) and asked if poss to get an umbrella near us she not only rolls her eyes than
walks away goes over to grab one next to 2 ladies and kept hitting their lounge chairs so they got up and moved aside and then she  slides it over to us not helping us place it between lounge chairs and walks away!!!??  The ladies next to us said - looks like she doesn't like her job!!!  We laughed it off and tried to enjoy the rest of the day but service didn't better or worse with pool attendant . 
 This is day 1 - that same evening we cancelled the Cabana for the following day and booked a cabana 
 at the W Hotel same price and great service !!  
We had reservations for their  restaurant that evening and most of us 8 girls ordered the steak after a long wait ( we were the only other table at this time 9:15pm) they came room temp at best but we decided not to send back however one was really rare and our friend who is pregnant couldn't eat it we asked if possible to cook it a bit longer the waitress said kitchen is closed I can microwave it  for you??!!!!! We suggested in the future not to tell a paying customer "buying a steak" to use the microwave??  When she brought the bill she slams the cup which had the bill on the table we noticed we were charged for desert we didn't get and says do you still want it??? We said not anymore but you still
Charged us ? she grabs gets upset grabs the bill and walks away... if we wouldn't have looked we would have been charged for something we didn't get?????? Gratuity was included but was not deserved ...  Day 2 we made it a point to not be at the hotel all day to avoid their poor service we came back for showers and called for a steamer which we were told they had and ice since both machines near us were broken. Needless to say they NEVER CAME.... We called 2 more times to check and front desk did NOT ANSWER  I truly just gave up!!
First thing Sunday morning  we checked out although we decided to stay in Scottsdale one more night there was no way they deserved another penny from us .  Wish we could have had 1 good experience to avoid a bad review.  NEVER AGAIN you lost 8 returning customers + some! 

We checked in at CENAHOUSE  - INCREDIBLE SERVICE  and PROFESSIONAL the Food/ staff/ rooms were perfect!!!!! 

The only thumbs up for the Scott's is to their valet staff the friendliest and nicest. Rocco thanks for your hospitality you were the best!!!!!

This is more of a Motel with good internet esthetics that's all don't let the pictures fool you. 
Read all reviews - wish we would have this hotel has downgraded a lot from our past visits. 
Brandon the General Manager has alot of work ahead to get this "hotel" to the 5 star mark or at least 4..... by the way we appreciated the sorry champagne sent to our room 2x they were left untouched, I would have rather have a good experience than a champagne bottle any day!!!

findings.title: Elizabeth M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I came here through ResortPass. I was expecting the usual overhyped hotel branded as a resort but I was so impressed that I had to share how excellent this place is. It's a well-kept secret that can easily hold its own among Scottsdale's finest. This is a location that has changed hands over the years--I was assuming it would be a bit rundown, but it was just the opposite--one of the best-maintained I've visited. The design of the lobby and the pool area were impeccable--modern and sedate but in fine fabrics. The lobby is huge, and I can see spending some time lounging there. The bathroom is cute and painted in a fun retro style, but with the tall doors you'd expect. The Canal Club food looked delicious as I passed by. The pool area was better than described. The jacuzzi is large--enough for strangers to comfortably share it. There were two pools, one of which was being cleaned with great attention to detail as I arrived. The towels were plush and distinctly designed. The pool I used was large, spacious enough to enjoy even if it's crowded. It was also well-heated--enough to use it very early in the morning. There was also another pool with a sandy beach area that slopes into the pool and then a more secluded pool. Even the uniforms of the servers showed great attention to style and detail. I will definitely return.

findings.title: Deanna Z. (4/5)
findings.snippet: This place is beautiful and so relaxing. I would recommend staying there. What I would not recommend is getting any food packages when you first book here. I did the chips, guacamole and pitcher of margaritas. First, I asked that it come at a certain time on a certain day. It came that day but hours later and we were not in our room. So when we came back chips were stale and ice was melted. Second, they charge this to your room. When I booked the room it was supposed to be a $50 package. When I got the bill it came to $66 and so I went to front desk. They said oh the additional amount is for taxes and room service!! That's a 32% increase!! To me that's false advertising and it should have been a flat fee of $50! That was the only disappointing thing. I just wouldn't do that again.

findings.title: Vivii L. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Although the dude at the front desk-- during check-in wasn't my cuppa tea-- Jessica (in the restaurant) made up the difference. I think they should reverse their roles and have her great folx with her knowledgeable, generous and authentically manner of engaging patrons. I felt seen by her, cared for, genuinely accommodated.

Overall--and what I'm about to say is saying A LOT given I'm currently on a cross-country road trip where I'm residing at "luxury" destinations. I use luxury loosely in some cases as I go in with an intention of openness and decide from the experience if in fact--luxury was a foot. #IYKYK... any who, I digress.

So, as I was saying the overall aesthetic of the SCOTT in Scottsdale, Arizona is a complete throwback to the highlife of 1920's Havana with a mid-century modern twist.

The diversity of staff, guests, and general attitudes (except of course the aforementioned front-desk-non-persona encounter,) is refreshing.

Loved the the first meal: a delicately prepared chef salad served with chicken so tender I was briefly concerned it wasn't cooked enough only to recognize it was cooked PERFECTLY and all the other chicken I'd previously consumed was actually suspect. The tres tacos were not only spicy, delicious, and presented with intention that wasn't lost on me or my guest, but they were actually warm and served via one tortilla versus the usual two, which, for me only adds more calories, carbs, and extra work to try and peel the extra tortilla away.... And the Arnold Palmer was more delicious than the one at Little Miss Bar-B-Que (which was the best I'd ever had before the one I had at the SCOTT.

And the I met Hailey--who is a boatload of PRETTY & PRECIOUS all rolled into one. She works in room service and knows how to beat a face like no other! Get it li'l mama! 

Although it cost me nearly $50 to have an order of avocado toast and almond butter toast delivered to my room... that... was... the... best damn toast I'd EVER had; like I'll drive all the way back here from the Bay Area for that almond butter/sesame seed/thick sliced nine grain tasting bread/perfectly sliced banana drizzled with honey & bee pollen deliciousness! Yeah... I said that.

Oh, and, instead of heading out and continuing my trip I decided to stay another day: it's too comfy to get back in car and drive especially given Fashion Square Mall is directly--directly enough--across the street!

Love this place. If I were EVER lucky enough yo be in love with someone who I wanted to marry and the feelings were EASILY mutual-- this place would rank high on my list for my bachelorette party weekend

Or.... If I were going to host a healing retreat for 50 wome to gather: I'd host it here

Love the   friendly part

findings.title: Jason M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We just went for our anniversary weekend and stayed for a work conference after that. Lovely property. Really liked the two pools and overall resort vibe around the pool area. I did yoga each morning at 8 a.m.  with yoga instructor Jodi. That was a real treat! Great gym. Peliton bike needs some repair. I forgot to share that with the front desk. So many great restaurants nearby and within walking distance. Highly recommend. I also took the complementary bikes for a long bike ride. The hotel offers a shuttle service around town but not to the airport.

findings.title: Cassie M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Came for a stay-bae-cation and enjoyed ourselves!! The hotel is super cute. The rooms have a lovely vibe. Chef Alex at the Canal Club absolutely crushed it. Dish after dish we were blown away. Great job!  Huge kudos to Aliana (probably spelled it wrong) at the front desk for the recommendation! Upon arrival last week, she was sweet and welcoming and made fantastic recommendations for things to do and places to eat for us the whole weekend. It appeared that they were low staffed and we watched her jump from one role to another our whole stay. We could see how hard she works. She definitely needs to be recognized for her efforts. However, we were taken back when we were leaving on Monday and we saw another staff named Along (probably spelled it wrong too), belittle Aliana, yell at her, and be overly rude to Aliana right in front of us and other guests. She might be a manager, I'm not sure. But she clearly has no management skills whatsoever. First, you never speak to an employee like that. Secondly, should you need to address something, you take them to the side away from guests. Third, Aliana was helping us because valet was full and the cars were backed up and no one would move. She was doing her job! If that was my daughter, I would have her file a lawsuit for abuse and a toxic work environment. No one ever deserves to have to work with that type of abuse, EVER. Overall, great stay but disappointed it was ruined at the end from a rude staff member. To HR: staff members sometimes can be a liability and it's obvious that Along is one of them. Cut your losses or you could lose more than customers. I am not sure if we'll be back as a result because vacation is not where I was to witness abuse on a young female. No thanks. There's too many nice resorts here in AZ to have to see that.

findings.title: Lee G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: If you have other options, stay elsewhere. Great aesthetics, but terrible service at restaraunt, front desk, and front desk manager.

findings.title: Irene B. (4/5)
findings.snippet: So glad we ended our week with a night here. I would not recommend staying here over the weekend if you are over 40. The pool was packed and it felt like a carnival cruise. However the area is beautiful and the rooms are really nice. Great staff. Lovely garden spot at the canal for dinner after dark and dinner salad and banana toast breakfast were memorable. A treat

findings.title: Agata K. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I came to the Scott Resort and Spa with my family for 6 nights to celebrate my birthday. Here are my thoughts:

Pros:
-Very clean, the lobby and exterior very pretty and aesthetic. Very instagramable. 
-Great location, walking distance to shopping and dining.
-Comfortable beds.

Cons: 

-We came towards the end of March, it was very packed with people. Lines in the lobby, no open outside seats. Long wait for service for Canal Club drinks/ food. 

-Not enough coffee in the room! They supply each room with a Nespresso machine that gives you one sip of coffee. We asked in the lobby if they have decaf aside from the rooms, the said no you have to go outside the resort to get it. Very disappointing. 

-Pool chairs, horrible experience. People get up early in the morning and reserve chairs with towels and leave it unattended for hours until they want to use it. I saw a sign that says that chairs can not be unattended for more than 30 min but staff does nothing about it.

findings.title: Jeanee B. (3/5)
findings.snippet: As an edit to a previous review, the management did hear our concerns and offer a fair resolution, which did go a long way.

findings.title: Simone J. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
in short version: do not come here. 

I have worked in the service industry for 7 years and believed anyone who wrote a negative review was too entitled with way too much time on their hands. After my experience here and seeing other negative reviews- I may need to change my previously held notion.

My husband and I came here for our honeymoon and it immediately started off terrible. We arrived at 4:15 (check in is 4pm) and we're told the room wasn't ready and we would be texted when it was. A text was never received so an hour later we walked up to the desk for an update. Magically, the room was ready. Frustrating that the room could have been ready earlier but nobody was paying attention. 

We would have let that slide but it continued to go down hill. We paid $50 to have a "fiesta celebration" (margs & chips) waiting for us in the room when we arrived. You guessed it- not there. My husband called and asked for one to be sent. 30 minutes pass, still not here. He walks up for the front desk and says it's on the way. Surprise, another 30 minutes. At this point I'm beyond frustrated because we drove 8 hours and skipped lunch thinking we'd be having this appetizer before our dinner reservation. I walk up to the front and tell them I will wait right here until someone brings it. Petty but necessary, and we still had to wait 15 more minutes. No apologies and I just paid $50 to carry my own drinks, chips & guac to my room, when I could have gotten it at the bar for half price. 

During this ordeal, the front desk girl kept going back and forth between the office and lobby to speak to her supervisor. Pretty terrible of the supervisor to know there is an issue but to simply remain sitting in the office, making the front desk worker attempt to handle an issue she has no authority to handle without manger approval. 

On to the room. We paid an extra $300 for a room that was advertised at "Lagoon View". Not even the smallest portion of the lagoon was visible from our room. Just a bush and a hammock. I typically do not care what the view is from my room when all the rooms are the same price- but to pay $300 more to not even get it, ridiculous. Of the five nights we were here, our room was cleaned once and that was simply because my husband called and requested it. 

This isn't a major issue but... questionable. When pulling up, the valet greeted and were helping unload the car. He saw a box of beer in the back and pulled one out and pretended to shotgun it. Not terrible, but far from professional. My issue wasn't him pretending to shotgun but him feeling comfortable enough to mess with our stuff. 


These weren't service issues due to a pandemic, but plain poor service. Definitely not even close to being worth nearly $600 a night. If your drawn into the lobby like I was when deciding where to book- you're better off just grabbing a drink at the bar but booking a different hotel.

findings.title: Grace S. (3/5)
findings.snippet: We stayed here 5 days. The grounds and lobby are absolutely beautiful! It is very well cared for and the rooms are fairly nice. Unfortunately we had multiple service issues during our stay. We called for towels twice and never received them, reserved a daybed at the pool and it was not set up/served at all, received incorrect food items, food service left in our room even after cleaning service, forgotten drinks that we had to ask about multiple times, etc. Overall, still beautiful and fun with the right people but absolutely did not feel worth the price!

findings.title: Jocelyn R. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
We booked through Hotels Tonight and then I looked at reviews which had me a bit nervous as they are all over the place.  We did enjoy our stay here overall, but had some of the same issues others have mentioned:

The Pros:

The staff we interacted with were all very nice
Comfy beds, enough towels, great water pressure
Super easy parking
Convenient to everything
The lobby really is *gorgeous*

The Cons:

Pretty pricey for the room size/condition
Sat at the outside restaurant for breakfast, nobody ever came by with water, coffee, anything, for a solid 15 minutes.  We left and went to Breakfast Club down the street and did not try eating at the Canal Club again.


Room turning - I'm mixed on this one (and not just here at The Scott).  I completely and totally get it, Covid and staffing issues, etc, and I know everybody is doing the best they can.  I don't even necessarily mind the every other day schedule on room turning, but I wish someone would TELL people that when they check in or leave a pamphlet in the rooms or something - it's such a downer to come back from a hike and realize you don't have any clean towels or coffee pods.  It feels like there's a middle ground here that all hotels could benefit from - I don't need you to vacuum my room or turn down my bed every day - just leave a bin with clean towels/cups/coffee pods outside and I will put the used stuff in it, easy peasy.  Surely someone can start adopting this happy medium approach eventually?

findings.title: Lisa L. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Don't judge a hotel by it's lobby!  What can I say, it's GORGEOUS.  The wow factor stops there.  It's like a girl with no substance.  I really wanted to love it.
Food is okay.  Alcohol selection is meh. Front desk girls are really nice and accommodating.

Let's talk about the room now.  It was just okay.

Let's get to the housekeeping, oh that's right, what housekeeping?  Room service dishes all up and down the hall for days (not hours).  When we asked why our room wasn't cleaned, they informed us it would be cleaned the following day (every other due to C19, say what?).  The following evening we came back to the same dirty room!  When my husband called the front desk, they said, oh...it should have been cleaned. Let us call you right back.  NO CALL BACK 30 min later.  I decided to clean myself, then let the front desk manager know what I thought about it.  Craziness.

Save your $$$!!!!  This is not resort style hospitality or luxury.

findings.title: Lowen S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I have called every department to try and speak with  someone and the phone keeps ringing. I've called the Canal club and left a voicemail and have not received a call back. Does anyone work here? If anyone does, please reach out to me so I can book a reservation. Thank you

findings.title: Sarah B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed for a 1/2 work 1/2 play trip. Great renovations, service, food and drink. Escaped NE winter and was delighted by this hotel. Picturesque grounds, meticulously manicured, and proximity to Scottsdale's offerings.

findings.title: T A. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
This resort is pretty. The food is nothing to write home about. The pool is cold. The sand-area off the pool is unpleasant due to crowding and the use of tiny rocks instead of sand.

The rooms are nice, but the pool is simply too crowded for families with small children or for people who like       space      to enjoy life--at least during the summer. This resort seemed like a place to see and be seen for the 20-35 age range.  I can appreciate that, but I was after a quiet day at the pool to read a book while my kiddo made sandcastles.

findings.title: Jean B. (3/5)
findings.snippet: We are at the resort as I type. My husband is here for a conference and I joined him. I need to work everyday but the WiFi is terrible! Difficult to connect, low signal, and drops the connection. Very, very frustrating. Front desk is of no help. So surprising that a hotel in the U.S. exists with such bad WiFi.

findings.title: Lizz P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Horrible service at the Canal restaurant. No one even recognized us for over 15 minutes. The server half heartily apologized and acted as if business as usual. I then got sick from the food. Will never go there again or even recommend the resort.

findings.title: Grant M. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Small resort ...
Old 1960's  
Poorly remodeled ... large
Closet should be bathroom which is too small 
Service marginal and for 700 plus a night you'd expect your bed to be made!  
So expensive and poor service

findings.title: Art D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Overall I had a great experience. I visited for a three day conference and they did a great job. The service and flexibility demonstrated by the staff was excellent.  Everyone was accommodating and friendly. The rooms are very nice and were cleaned every other day. Communicating with the staff was easy because they send you a text once checked in and you can use that to ask questions and their response time is prompt! 

The food at the conference I found was pretty good and managed very well. Plenty of people around to assist and clean quickly after you finished eating. 

The bar area say's open late and you are able to meet a people at the bar or sit in an area with you and your party peacefully as well. 

Overall great experience and would recommend. I checked in on a Monday and out on a Thursday, total cost was. $1.1K that included one meal at the bar of $35. 

Now for eye candy. Well did not see much of that. The pool area is very nice and looks like there is some potential. However, the resort is not very big in comparison to others I have attended but is is sufficient.

findings.title: Hal M. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
For a convention or large group event, like a business meeting or a wedding, The Scott in Scottsdale, AZ is a nice venue. The dining room is nice and the staff is friendly and accomodating. There are fire pits in several locations and the pool and jacuzzi are inviting.
That being said, I would not recommend this hotel if you are going for a four star, as advertized, hotel room. Despite the nice balcony off the room and a nice view from it, my wife and I, upon entering the room, were shocked at its poor condition and its small size. The room did have new carpet and a nice T.V., but the bed was way too soft for anyone with a back issue, the bathroom, with a single sink was large enough for only one small person, it had sloppy caulking around the shower drain and between the tiles, the knob to turn the water on needed repair. There were no drawers or extra space for toiletries. The living room lacked a dresser with drawers. There was only a small closet for hanging a few items, which was the only place in the room for unpacking. 
Additionally, the furniture was old, tattered and in need of repair. By the way, housekeeping only comes every other day unless you call for service. Another disappointment was the noise. Since there were large events help at this hotel, the music was turned up full blast, which is what one would expect, ok, but all the glass throughout the hotel, including the rooms, had single pane windows. Nowhere  could you find  piece and quiet while the D.J. cranked up the music. My wife have stayed in hundreds of hotels around the globe and can safely say this hotel was at the lower end of the list. By the way, were charged $559 a night for what I would call "two star" accommodations.  If you want a really classy, comfortable and well maintained hotel on your next visit to Scottsdale, do yourself a favor and look for another venue, there are plenty from which to choose.

findings.title: John W. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This review is for anyone thinking of booking The Scott for a business or large event like a wedding. Take your business elsewhere! In November, my company had booked meetings at the hotel for four nights this month. When the Omicron variant struck two of our attendees were exposed to the virus. To avoid risking all of our leadership team from being exposed, which would devastate our business, we had to cancel. Although we were told this is a small family run business, we were left to talk to two middle management sales people who had no empathy or customer service. We were told that the most that could be done was to give us credit for $5k of $26k spent, but the credit would only apply if we spent another $26k total on the future event.  We asked for a full credit toward a future event and they said no. They didn't care that we would be repeat customers as we do these meetings annually. So warning to anyone thinking of this hotel or any other property owned by this group in Arizona and California, don't book your meeting or event here.  You have many better choices. My company will never give this hotel chain our business again, and I will continue to spread the word to avoid this hotel.

findings.title: Sam G. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I stayed for one night. A lovely resort with clean rooms a beautiful pool spa and all the things necessary for a great time. I suggest booking during the week or calling ahead to determine if there are special events going on at the resort. I had a couple hiccups at my stay but the manager Aaron, professionally and politely corrected the issues. Again I would recommend staying there, but perhaps you'd like to call ahead and understand if there any special events hosted. Great location

findings.title: Melissa S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
This iconic Scottsdale Boutique hotel has outlived it prime! Let me start by saying what a lovely welcoming front entrance with the classic car and bicycles. The Lobby was beautiful with its Havana vibe. The front desk staff was welcoming, and check in was prompt. 
We went to room 116, and were please with the size, layout and decor, but it was quite weathered. The shower had poor drainage and there was a loud and constant whirring noise (not associated w the A/C), keeping us awake all night...even noise canceling AirPods with music could not block the noise. They move our room at 5 am. Room 550, consistently decorated. We had not tried the A/C until bedtime (our bad), now we had a different, and even louder noise. Exhausted from the day we turned it off for the night but the room got stuffy. Back to reception...maintenance fixed the A/C, no more noise, but not blowing cold air any longer. There was a room service tray on the floor in the hall for 24+ hours.
Taking advantage of the live music and energy of The Canal club after returning from dinner we found the service to be horribly understaffed. Couldn't order a second round and unbussed tables all around the lobby, we had to search someone out to pay.
SO DISAPPOINTING.... Don't waste your money.

findings.title: Lisa O. (2/5)
findings.snippet: NO HEAT! OVERPRICED! This place has a nice lobby and pool area, however the rooms are horrible. Low ceilings, small, dark bathrooms, old beds! There were huge stains on the hallway carpet which looked like vomit. The beds seemed very old and creaked and sunk when you got in them. Terribly uncomfortable!!! The rooms are like a 2-3 star motel at best. Everything is old. Shower had mold and mildew. There is a creepy painting of some lady in the bathroom who "stares" at you when you shower... strange vibe. I would not sit on the sofa in the room because the fabric looked so dirty I couldn't imagine what kind of germs were on there. Worst of all, it was 37 degrees outside and there was NO HEAT in our room!!! The "heater" blew only cold air! We called and a staff member came and verified the heat was broken. We moved all our stuff to another room only to find there was no heat in that room, either.... plus, there was a horrible loud, high pitched hissing sound coming from the vent!!!  Sounded like an animal was stuck in there. According to the front desk staff, the engineer "was not on site", so we ended up moving BACK to our original room since at least there was no hissing sound.  This place is understaffed, overpriced, and run down. I seriously wanted to leave. By the way, when they quote the room price they don't tell you about the $45 resort fee. I might visit the lobby for a drink but will never stay overnight again! Shout out to Megan at the front desk who was very pkeant and professional despite being completely unsupported by her employer!

findings.title: Katie D. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We had a quick lovely stay here at the newly renovated Scott Resort which used to be a Kimpton property. 
First impressions are that this place knows high end service: the interior lobby is beautiful with a sort of Miami vibe and the grounds are quite lovely. 
I had asked about price matching and it doesn't appear they do that - at least not for Hotel Tonight? Seemed a little strange to me considering most hotel chains encourage you to book directly and inquire about price matching. We ended up paying much more than I would have through HT (about $100+ or so), but the check in clerk upgraded our room since we booked direct. We did very much appreciate that. 
Our 15 pound cutie of all cutiest dog stayed with us. Fees for pups are $100 per visit; I'd say it's worth it if you stay multiple nights. 
The room was beautiful and clean. We loved the decor very much. And the bed... oooo it was wonderful. 
Where I think there is room for improvement would be the staff at the Cabana Club who all seemed very green - tables were not bussed (I'd say more than half had dirty plates left on them) and the cocktails weren't made well or the recipe needed improvement on the Paloma. But the bartender was attentive and patient, allowing me to taste the different red wines (selection was v nice). 
All things considered, I'd stay here again. It's walking distance to Nobu, the Scottsdale Fashion Square and many other yummy restaurants. Wish I had taken more photos to share with you!

findings.title: Desirae B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Such a beautiful resort. The ambience is super nice and the rooms were really are done! Definitely a higher up 4 star hotel!

findings.title: William M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Had a good time on our little staycation. Service was good, Canal Club was great and great seating area by the fire. Bedrooms were nice and cozy. Beds did make creaking sounds from my wife and I having a good time, so sorry for the people next to us all night. Other than that a great stay!

findings.title: Autumn C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
When I say a picture is not always what it seems, that is exactly what I found with this resort. I do a lot of staycations and the management is awful here. They brought me back for a " bad experience " but chose to have me sleep in a room right next to the dumpsters looking at a cement wall! I left a day early and no one even noticed. You'd think they would make sure the stay was a good one the second time around. 

It was so pleasant to wake up to the garbage truck at 6am ! 

Needless to say I don't have a lot to say !

findings.title: Karin H. (3/5)
findings.snippet: The grounds and lobby are incredible, but the service is just okay and EVERYTHING except for the room is a la carte. A very expensive stay.

findings.title: Shahe K. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
This place Beyond Sucks!!!

Service sucks!!
Room service Sucks!!
Front desk Sucks!!
The canal club staff sucks!!

Ordered coffee two mornings in a row, no show, no coffee! Called the front desk, they said no problem, we will have it up to you shortly???? CRICKETS!!! STILL WAITING!!!

My room door had a sign that said privacy please!


But, while my wife is changing and i am on the balcony, the service help just opens the door
and comes into the room to leave a robe we had requested a while back. 

NO KNOCK, NO SOUND, JUST OPEN THE DOOR AND COME ON IN!! WTF!!!???


The property and theme is ok but not thrilling!! We stayed for 2 nights and both nights we left to go somewhere else to eat and drink!!! That's how bad this place is!!!

Stay clear of this shit hole and go someplace else!!

findings.title: Stacey M. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Facilities were grossly understaffed (or at least the staff on hand could not handle the volume). For such a pricy, supposed "4 star resort", I was extremely disappointed. And honestly - I felt sorry for the staff. They seemed completely unsupported. I can give some specific examples. For starters, the check-in area is tiny and cannot handle large groups. Bad layout. On a busy Saturday, the Kitchen Manager apparently stopped all food orders at the Canal Club bar so nobody could order any food from the bar. Drinks were also pretty backed up, but again they seemed understaffed and the bartender was doing the best she could and friendly. The restaurant hostess, on the other hand, was rude and unprofessional. We approached her for seating and she was on her phone and we had to get her attention. We were told it was a 30min wait, even though there were tons of open tables. A couple after us was told 10min and when I questioned her she said, "I thought there were 4 of you", which there were clearly only 2 of us standing there. No waitress EVER came to our table and after 20min we went and hunted one down. They were also very overwhelmed and explained there were no sections assigned and they didn't know we'd been seated (again- hostess fail, but still they should have checked on us). Once we finally got our food, it was very good but I wouldn't say worth all the hassle and wait time. The only real positive thing I have to say is check out was very easy and there was a very friendly, helpful man that worked on getting us a car; very professional and constantly updating us. He gets a gold star, but the resort management gets a giant thumbs down.

findings.title: Keri G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Korin was amazing! She was personable and her service was impeccable... Gorgeous area and perfect weather too!

findings.title: Megan S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We came here for dinner on a Friday night and we're sat right away for a table for 2! Highly recommend sitting at their bar for a cocktail, but the Cuban food is so bomb. Great views, excellent service, and amazing food. The steak or cubano is our top choice!

findings.title: Stephani Y. (5/5)
findings.snippet: So! We wanted to stay here unfortunately they were booked but I still came in to their spa for a facial! And let me tell you!!!! It was the cutest spa I have ever seen!!!! I go to the Ritz all the time but I loved the vibe and service here 1000 times more! My esthetician Julianna was so amazing! The front desk staff were so polite and sweet! It was the best experience by far! I would love to try the hotel next time!

findings.title: Alec L. (4/5)
findings.snippet: We loved it here!! Had a great stay excellent time! Pool service could have more staff is my only reason for 4 stars. Other than that can't wait to come back

findings.title: Lori J. (3/5)
findings.snippet: The Scott offers 4.5 star looks/aesthetic and price for a 2.5-3 start value. My room was a bit musty and I saw 5 bugs throughout my 3 night stay. This wasn't too bothersome and understanding since we were on the first floor. Pool side and Canal bar have great drinks, however they were out of ingredients for a few of their cocktails all weekend, and they were short staffed. For the price of a facial, I was expecting a full service spa, however it was not. Banquet food was not good at all. Some of the conference attendees skipped dinner on the second night because of this. All and all we got some good pics but not the best value for what you'll pay.

findings.title: Marie R. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I expected sooo much more from this hotel from all the pictures I've seen. My little family and I stayed for a night just to check out the place. The lobby was super cute and aesthetically pleasing. But that's literally it. The rooms were gross. Our room was right on the corner so maintenance was constantly driving around and was super loud. The room def needed to be upgraded. The food was okay as well. We checked out pretty early the next day because I just wanted to get out of there. For the price to stay there, it wasn't worth it at all.

findings.title: Jessica L. (1/5)
findings.snippet: This place is disgusting. They have a beautiful lobby for pics but the rooms are DISGUSTING. Our door didn't even work. Someone couldn't easily stolen all our things. The room next to us left at 2 am because they were trapped inside their room. Our sink didn't drain.  Our AC literally didn't work. AND WE PAID FOR THE NICEST SUITE. The pool is an actual joke. Very tiny. Worst one of all the resorts in Scottsdale. The Spanish speaking crew (clearly not knowing we spoke Spanish) was laughing about a gigantic cockroach while we were checking out.. The place is hyped up Bc it has a beautiful lobby.  Hit us with extra charges at checkout with no proof, even after we complained about the poor room. I'd only recommend this to place to my enemies.

findings.title: Ralph A. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My sister and I have come here for 17+ years. It was always sparkling and magnificent and low-key with lots of quiet and space. Lodgers came to relax, yes, have a drink, but not obnoxiously. Since their new ownership it has become ordinary and annoying. Amazingly, they took down the stunning Fire Pits, with waterfalls that were on towers over the main pool. For the last 4 years we found it overrun with people: several large, loud-partying heavy-drinking groups. There was low/no availability of chaise lounges. If you're looking for a quiet restful spa-like environment, this is not it anymore. We need to find our new "heaven".

findings.title: Megan C. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
The property looks nice, but the service inside and at the pool was awful. We went to brunch and waited for service for over 20 minutes. We tried to order brunch and they said "sorry its now closed and we don't want the chefs to yell at us.," We could of order brunch if they actually acknowledge us. Afterwards we went to the pool and they had 2 servers and a bartender. They took 50 minutes to finally come over. The pool wasn't busy and the servers (girls) were all on their phones the whole time. Even at one point I stood at the bar waiting for service while she was on her phone and then asked if I could order. I told the bartender that we would order food so please have the servers come over.......they then still didn't show up until 30 minutes. I work in hospitality and this would never fly.

8/16/21

findings.title: Krys M. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My fiancé and I booked this "Resort" as a quick 3 day get away. I researched The Scott and based off reviews and pictures it seemed like a very nice resort and worth the nightly rates. Unfortunately it was the opposite. When we arrived the first red flag was the stench in the hallways and the room. It smelled as if it had not been sanitized or cleaned properly in months. Although I brushed it off as the resort is just very old and needs to be updated. Shortly after, we found long strands of hair in the bathroom sink. I really wanted to enjoy our stay so we looked past that as well. Day 1 was spent mostly away from the hotel as we were exploring the city. Day 2 was a mess. We got up early to grab something to eat from the on site restaurant and was told they were not serving food on the property due to having only one cook in the kitchen and that guest must leave the property to go find food. And when I asked if I could make reservations for later the two young lady host stated with a smirk that they couldn't reserved anything at the moment. So with no choice we went off the property to find food. Throughout the day I noticed how untidy the lobby area, pool, and walk way around the stairs to the rooms were. At multiple times there was leftover food and dirty dishes sitting on the lobby tables which left no desirable place to sit. The pool area was dirty and not maintained and the staff paid no attention to the guest. To top it off the balcony was full of moths throughout the day so we couldn't sit out there as well. We were forced to spend day 2 in the room.  At this point this resort felt more like a 3 star hotel and not a resort. We decided to check out early. Our money and time off work to fly in to experience Arizona was a complete waste and disappointment.

findings.title: Gary P. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Check in was late. The room had a very rank odor. The pool was filthy dirty in the afternoon, evening and morning. The room location and view were not as booked. Seating for breakfast was refused even though dining room was less than 10% occupied. Late check out was available at booking but front desk charged $25 per hour. We would definitely not recommend!!!

findings.title: Kathy H. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
#1.  WATCH FOR CHARGES ON YOUR CREDIT CARD #you leave for incidentals.  You will be wrongfully charged, over charged, charged twice. Then you'll get a short argument. Then an apology and have to wait for the credit back to your card! 

#2.  ASK FOR A RECEIPT when you check out!   We were charged for 4 nights instead of 1 on my room. 3 nights were paid for in advance, then one night was added and they told me to pay at check out.  FIRST my phone started dinging, They charged me for all 4 nights,  Again.  Then Stephan, the Director, argued with me, for at least 15 minutes, basically calling me a liar, making me raise my voice.  He went to read, out loud, the list of the names of prepaid rooms, quickly reading them to prove that I wasn't on the list, "Yvonne! Sue! Sandy! Paulino! Kathy!  Oh, there you are".  Voice lowered, "Sorry for the confusion".   Yes, I was on "the list".  He had the girl on the next counter change places with him for her to take care of me.  Director Stephan, before you start telling a guest they are wrong, before you start arguing, I highly suggest, get your facts straight first.  

#3.  If you need something extra like a broom or cleanup (spilled coffee grounds) don't hold your breath. We asked for a broom to sweep it ourselves, for 2 days. They never showed.  
We had an event and requested trashs bags.  2 days, they never brought them.  We hunted some down from the maintenance. 

#4. One of the attendees' tires were stolen over night off their truck.

GOOD STUFF ..  The servers in the banquet hall were all nice and helpful. 

Especially for a big event, the meals were delicious.  The desserts were wonderful too. 

Housekeeping staff were very nice. 

The bartenders at our event were very nice. 

The maintenance people were very nice .

The beds and pillows are comfy!!

The area of Old Town Scottsdale is nice for out of state visitors to be able to walk around and explore and shop.

findings.title: Joel M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: All is quite perfect except wet people crossing lobby from swimming pool  to rest rooms

findings.title: Lil S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I tried booking a couple's massage here and first of all the lady I spoke with was extremely rude and short with me, despite this it was the only place I could find that was allowing couples massages lately  so I still tried to book an appointment. Everything seemed fine until they told me that after 20% tip the total would be $350 and there were no saunas, hot tubs, pools, or any sort of accommodations. Just a massage. And just so you know that's $291 for both of us without tip, $145.50 each for a massage. For the rude customer service and lack of facilities anyone can agree that's generously overpriced. Never coming here.

findings.title: Sarah A. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The service Benjamin at the Canal Club provide is a reason to come in for a visit. He really goes the extra mile the other reviewers are spot on! 

Today I had the Cuban sandwich and the was crusty, pork savory & the sauce and jalapeño pickles really just made my whole afternoon. 

Immediately when you walk into the lobby your swept away into their beautifully designed interior  full of foliage and plenty of gorgeous seating. A short stroll forward and the  pool is sparkling and inviting just like their online photos! Will be back soo,

findings.title: Ames J. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Save your money, not worth it!
Pros: aesthetically beautiful lobby, that's it!!
Cons:poor customer service, long waits for service at restaurant(we waited OVER 1 hour for our food AFTER they said it is being plated), pool service closes at 5pm, pools are dirty!!! Small bottled water is $7!
The only friendly staff were bartenders at The Canal.
Definitely not worth your money, there are plenty of other nicer places nearby with much better service and staff

findings.title: Damien C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This review is for the spa - it is an absolute must! My wife and I came here for a little stay-cation for our anniversary and we were both very impressed by the the level of attention, friendliness and service brought by our massage therapists, who I believe were both named Michelle. We both came out very relaxed, and the champagne and truffles at the end were an added bonus!

findings.title: Kylie S. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful place but I feel like their workers are unhappy. We were at the pool seated kind of close to the bar and all the waitresses could talk about was how awfulness a place it was. They were swearing and dropping f bombs all over the place it was hard to relax. They had such bad attitudes. They just saytheir gossiping. We had to move. Very unprofessional and killed the vibes of our stay. It happened both days at the pool.

findings.title: Thankyou S. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The lobby is super nice, could've hung out there all night. The pools are great too, but were littered with trash when we went out for a swim (around 8:30p or 9p). While I was initially shocked by all the garbage, a staff member had cleaned up the entire area within 5-10mins of our swim. The pools were beautiful and the gardens in courtyard were A+. The room we had was large and well decorated. The seating area was not really useful as there was giant wicker lighting fixture hanging directly in front of your face. It was a cool fixture, but it didn't fit.  

The room we had was a deal, and it get worth every penny. They charge for pretty much everything in the room, so we didn't mess with any of that. $5 for a mini bar can of coke, yeah no thanks. You gotta be blackout drunk to pay for that. Also $25 for condoms and lube, gross.

Will be back!

findings.title: Kelli M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Went to the Scott for a bachelorette weekend and had the best time! The room was clean and very stylish but we all had the best time at the pool. A huge shoutout to Jocelyn and Emily for being so wonderful and providing excellent service! Also, Kourtney at the bar was so nice! I can't wait to come back!

findings.title: Amber E. (5/5)
findings.snippet: As much as we love The Strawberry Inn, we're travel junkies at heart and LOVE visiting other boutique hotels and learning all we can. That's why we jumped at the opportunity to have a little stay-cation at The Scott Resort & Spa. The Scott is unique in that while it is part of a group of hotels (Classic Group and Hotels), each hotel has a completely unique design, and is managed directly by Classic Group to give each guest a beautiful botique experience! We loved our stay- highly recommend!

findings.title: Rachel G. (2/5)
findings.snippet: My husband booked us a stay for my birthday. He paid extra to have champagne and chocolate dipped strawberries upon our arrival. It never came so I think they're removing the charge, we'll see. He scheduled a couples massage for us, which was supposed to be 50 minutes, it was only about 35 minutes for about $350. On our first day we had breakfast at the Canal Club and asked to sit outside. The server told us that only large parties could be seated outside. Then we watched three different groups of two just walk in and seat themselves outside. When I asked the server about it she said, "well you can't please everyone". On day two, we came back to our room to find that housekeeping had not come by. When we called the front desk, we were told that they don't do daily housekeeping. So we asked to have some towels and Nespresso pods delivered. They never came so my husband walked to the front desk to ask again. Finally they were delivered. The poolside cocktail server Jocelyn(?) was fairly rude, at one point she (literally) tossed the check onto my husband's lap and said "here ya go", even after we had tipped her 12-15% each day on +$130 bill. There was a group of underage "adults" sitting next to us. They came in with a backpack full of truly/white claws, taking up 5-6 chaise lounges and talking about how they were only 19 years old and that "clearly they don't care here". Why did we spend $150 a day on watery cocktails when these kids brought their own drinks for free? I didn't find out about daily yoga or the cute bikes until we were checking out. The scent of the lobby is amazing, the decor is the cutest, but unless you want to be run over by Instagrammer's suitcases (this also literally happened), don't bother. There was a bartender inside with a shaved head who was awesome, but other than that staff acted as if they were grounded with their phones taken away. Generally speaking, The Scott knows that people are going to flock to them because the grounds are super cute and Instagrammable, they also know that some negative reviews for service, etc aren't going to affect their revenue. Quantity versus quality I guess. My advice, stay somewhere else and just pop in for a cocktail.

findings.title: Helena S. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Was super excited about staying here as the pictures on their website depict a boho resort that's absolutely beautiful. However, this was not what we experienced. In our first room we started experiencing a very pungent smell which was unknown... we then were moved into a second room. This room was by far worse as we dealt with unwashed sheets that had mascara stains and hair leftover from the previous guests. Then as we were removing the sheets from the bed we noticed urine stains on the duvet insert then a giant urine spot on the mattress protector which looked as it had never been cleaned. In addition both rooms bathrooms's showers had hair that was clogging the drain which appeared it had not been properly cleaned...
